amendment-a.title: Publishing proposed constitutional amendments
amendment-a.summary: Constitutional Amendment A would replace the requirement that proposed constitutional amendments be published in newspapers in every county with a publication method set by state law. Under the implementing statute, the full text of proposed amendments and other legislative ballot questions would be posted on the Utah Public Notice Website and the Lieutenant Governor's website for 60 days before the general election. The amendment would take effect January 1, 2027, if approved.
amendment-a.for_means: A vote FOR means the Constitution would no longer require newspaper publication of proposed amendments, and publication would instead follow state law, including posting the full text online for 60 days before the general election.
amendment-a.against_means: A vote AGAINST means the Constitution would continue to require publication of proposed amendments in a newspaper in each county where one is published, for two months before the general election.

amendment-b.title: 60% voter approval for certain statewide tax initiatives
amendment-b.summary: Constitutional Amendment B would require statewide citizen-proposed laws that increase taxes compared to existing law to be approved by at least 60% of voters rather than a simple majority. It would cover initiatives that create a new tax, expand an existing tax, increase a tax rate, or change a property tax rate so that it decreases less than current law would. Other statewide initiatives would continue to require a simple majority, and the change would apply to initiatives voted on after November 1, 2026.
amendment-b.for_means: A vote FOR means statewide citizen-proposed laws that increase taxes would need approval from at least 60% of voters to become law. Other statewide initiatives would still need a simple majority.
amendment-b.against_means: A vote AGAINST means statewide citizen-proposed laws that increase taxes would continue to need only a simple majority of voters to become law.
